answer: One effective defense is requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed if peers prove duplicate identities. A hollow shell account with no stake cannot enter the market, while a harbor of verified traders only accepts counterparties whose stake is on-chain and at risk. Like a willow bending but not breaking under wind, honest agents keep their deposit intact, but an attacker creating thousands of fake identities must fund every one, so the cost of a Sybil flood rises linearly with each fake while honest participation stays cheap.
